content.title: About
content.content: Burrito with beans and cheese is a Mexican dish consisting of a large soft wheat tortilla filled with cooked beans, melted cheese, and sometimes additional vegetables and spices. The tortilla is usually made from wheat flour, and the filling makes the dish hearty and protein‑rich.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The burrito originated in North Texas in the early 1920s and quickly spread throughout Mexico and the United States.
Beans used are often black or pinto, providing high fiber and slow‑release energy.
Cheese in traditional recipes is usually cheddar or Mexican “queso” that melts into a creamy texture.
Burritos are hand‑held, making them popular for on‑the‑go meals and picnics.
Variations may include rice, avocado, salsa, sour cream, and even grilled meat.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Beans and cheese together provide a substantial amount of protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Beans supply both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar stability.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: Beans are a good source of iron and magnesium, which aid oxygen transport and nerve‑muscle function.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The burrito provides B1, B6, and folate, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The tortilla, cheese, and beans make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant; lactose‑free alternatives can be used.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese and ready‑made sauces often contain a lot of salt, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Bean allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to beans and should choose different fillings.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are typically served hot. Heat them in a microwave or skillet, then fold tightly and eat with your hands. Add salsa, guacamole, or sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months; reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
